title: fix(sse): stable streaming framing and partial-JSON handling (delimiter + token/event ordering)
author: Aisha Patel
description: Fixes a class of SSE streaming bugs that caused truncated/invalid partial-JSON payloads and out-of-order token/event framing when chunks split delimiters or token-event boundaries. Motivation: customer incident ENG-4121 and internal canary failures showed two edge cases: (1) delimiters ('\n\n' and JSON delimiter tokens) being split across TCP frames caused the parser to treat partial JSON as complete, resulting in invalid final payloads; (2) when tokenized events were emitted concurrently with structured metadata events, ordering between token events and high-level 'done'/'delta' events could be non-deterministic under batching. Changes: robust framing state machine that keeps delimiter state across chunk boundaries; explicit token/event queue with sequence numbers for in-order replay; fallback merging strategy for partial JSON objects across multiple chunks; OpenAI-compat adapter updates so compatibility layer emits ordered events and retains SSE chunk boundaries for downstream SDKs. Implementation touches framer and parser in the runtime, the openai compatibility adapter, and SDK shims. Testing: added unit tests covering delimiter-split across chunk boundaries, property-based fuzzing for chunk reassembly, integration e2e that replays captured production traces from ENG-4121. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag sse.strict_framing with canary on 10% of traffic for 48h, then full roll. Checklist: link linear ENG-4121; add unit and integration tests; add e2e regression harness; enable feature flag for canary; monitor canary metrics and error budgets. Note: no API contract changes; this is backwards-compatible for existing SSE consumers but fixes cases where they saw invalid JSON or misordered events.

review_comments: Marco Liu: Please make framing state machine deterministic across goroutine boundaries; observed nondeterminism in earlier prototype. A: addressed by moving sequence increment into single-threaded framer loop and adding tests.

Priya Singh: Can we preserve original chunk boundaries for SDKs that rely on them? A: openai compatibility adapter now preserves chunk metadata and emits ordered events while retaining original chunk boundary markers.
James O'Connor: Add more fuzz tests around delimiter splits and very large payloads. A: added property-based fuzzing and expanded regression traces.
